correctness.rationale: The proof verifies normalization over every odd good-characteristic field, derives the distinct critical-point ordinary nodes, identifies each of 2δ normalization parameters as exactly one of δ explicit root-of-unity branch pairs, and computes arithmetic Frobenius on those pairs. Node local-unit tori carry integral signed permutation modules; one-branch infinity contributes no torus. Signed orbit decomposition yields genuine Weil-restriction and norm-one torus isomorphisms, then extension counts and zeta. A standalone exact checker independently tests 1471 label types, 498 prime-field and 162 quadratic-field point counts, including the nontrivial (3,8,7) case; finite tests do not replace universal proof.

originality.rationale: Verified claims/implications of the direct 2008/2009 plane Chebyshev geometry, 2011 equal-degree arrangement paper and three closest published results. The previously published same-curve finite-field theorem is restricted to two signed congruences, whereas this statement has mixed q-Frobenius orbit lengths for all unit residues and proves the actual integral torus decomposition. The (3,8,7) example is outside prior signed hypotheses. Residual unindexed-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed arithmetic Chebyshev-curve or knot-projection treatments might give equivalent all-residue signed-orbit formulas under different terminology.

The 2014 finite-field trigonometric Chebyshev polynomial chapter was only identified through bibliographic/abstract discovery and not fully read; specific coverage of generalized Jacobian tori remains unverified.
The classification has not been independently validated and source searches are not a global uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: A complete arithmetic classification for the natural family of maximally nodal coprime Chebyshev plane curves. It recovers earlier special signed cases, fills the all-residue gap in full extension-field zeta factors and computes integral Picard-torus isomorphism types not recoverable from mere rational eigenvalues. The (3,8,7) example contains both negative fixed nodes and positive quadratic node orbits, demonstrating genuinely new structure.
